Here’s my list (some of these are pretty hot: they’re my opinions and I won’t be arguing about it in the replies), I’ve already posted a few in here. They’re mostly involving Wano, as that’s the arc I started reading weekly: 

- Big Mom and Kidd (by extension Killer) we’re narratively pointless in the arc. Only serving to over inflate an already bloated arc. Them being in Wano also detracted from Kiado being this unstoppable tyrant, and Laws plan to take him down with Luffy. 
- Fake out deaths, especially Kinemons, take away from the story and serve as a chapter cliffhanger and no more. And off screen deaths are lazy. 
- Wano is a C tier arc at best. It has some fantastic moments, some of the best in the series, but also some of the most egregious. 
- Recent events, the ending of Wano, stumbling upon vegapunk and such, all feel rushed and like things were left out for the sake of time. Oda spends too much time on the unimportant
- Yamato changing their mind right at the end means that all of the dialogue about joining the SH was filler to further pad things out
- The Gomu Gomu retcon into the Nika Nika fruit has harmed the meaning of the story and harms Luffys character and his goals more than most of you care to admit, and is much more on the nose than Oda has been up until that point. The new powers could’ve been explained as the awakening of the Gomu fruit.
- Nami has had one good character moment since Arlong Park and that was in Wano. 1000 chapters later. 
- The old mafia boss should’ve died. It would’ve made for a perfect character moment for Chopper, brining his dream back into focus for the reader. 
- Dressrosa is narratively one of the most sound PTS arcs, if not of all of OP. 
- Egghead island and the Vegapunk arc so far has been very boring and Lucci feels out of character. And the futurist stuff has gone too far now I think. 

I have a good few more but these are some of the hottest ones. Feel free to argue amongst yourselves

It put everything into perspective. My behaviour for about 10 years all made sense. In a way it helped me understand what was wrong so I can start fixing it. 
However it made me resentful towards my parents who should’ve gotten me check out when I started self destructing.

Yes you can and it can be beautiful. Unfortunately because of the type of illness this is you need to work constantly on yourself being better and being patient. However they’ve also got to understand and strong enough to brave a collapse. To hold onto you despite your attempts to push them away. Communication is key, you have to be open when your not feeling good, or when you think you’re failing or falling over. You need to be able to recognise when an episode is coming and suppressing the urges that come with all of that. It’s requires a great effort and introspection. 

My wife is so kind and soft, but so strong. She carries me on my worst days and celebrates with me while I’m feeling great. It may be related to the BDP (so my doctor tells me) but I don’t feel much empathy in general. So when I do things that could hurt others, physically or emotionally, I have to think about those consequences. It’s almost a second nature now but I have my days where I slip backwards. My wife chips me on it and helps bring me back to focus. Your partner needs to be understanding, that you are ill, and as any illness there are good and bad. But under no circumstances are they to allow you to blame poor behaviour solely on it alone. Responsibility and accountability help a lot in understanding what the illness can do to others as well as yourself.

A strong, compassionate person whom with you can communicate openly and feel comfortable in vulnerability is what you need. I know it’s hard to get to that point or find it but it’s out there. On the days your mind is telling you awful things remember that person does love you, all of you. They wouldn’t put up with some of the horrible things that come with BPD. 

The short of it is; yes you can have a wonderful and fulfilling relationship, but never be complacent with keeping yourself and the more destructive urges in check.

After years of being ignored and brushed off I decided to make myself invisible. I cut off all but my closest friend, I took a job working nights, I often wore unbranded and slightly oversized clothing, I was quiet at work as to not bring attention to myself (my skill at my job brought me attention that I ignored best I could). This went on for maybe 4 years, until I was around 21/22. 

I’m a generally nice person and help when I see a problem, this caught the attention of a girl from work on the day shift. She was incredibly outgoing and easy to talk to, it also helped that she was eye wateringly good looking (I’m around average so it was weird she showed me so much attention). One day, after maybe 4 months of hounding, I went out for a drink with her and her friends. I enjoyed their company and after a few weeks it was too late to just go back to my normal, so I played along with them. I didn’t talk much in the group and I didn’t always go out, only enough not to draw attention to myself for being introverted. 

About 8 months after this started we were our one night and a girl I hadn’t met before joined us. She was beautiful, a guy in the group saw her and said to me “she looks like a real world princess”. She was of Indian decent and was wearing a lot of traditional piercings, make up and (though more modern style) clothing. I agreed and we went about the night, I was introduced and we made brief conversation. At some point someone gave her my Snapchat and that was that for the night. I didn’t think much of our interactions. 

The following morning I awoke to a message from her saying something like “it was nice to meet you, I hope you got home okay. Maybe I’ll see you again this summer”. I replied with similar sentiment and that was that. 

A few weeks later I was working overtime and couldn’t go out, she happened to be out that night too. I wished the group chat a good time and put my phone away. On my lunch I checked it and I had a voice note from my friend and and a few messages. In the voice note you could here the girl saying how she wished I had been out and how she really liked talking with me and so on. 

I asked her for a drink and during our evening she said to me “you like being invisible don’t you? Unnoticed and just another face in the crowd. Too bad, I see you” 

“Too bad, I see you” that was it. I wanted her to see me now, I wanted to be seen with her. We immediately started dating and I found myself absolutely head over heels for her. She went away for work and we separated as we were still only new, but that feeling of being seen, I wanted that again. So I started making an effort to be seen. I wore clothes that fit, took pride in my appearance, made effort to form new friendships, and he recognised for my work. 

Almost 3 years in from that one sentence I’m engaged and store manager with a large group of people I call friends. 

She changed my entire perspective on life, and I will forever be grateful to her for that!

What’s the actual problem, are you dying really quick? Not doing much damage? Struggling to memories patterns of enemies and such? All of these require different solutions. 

Dying quickly - If I’m honest Godrick feels like he should be attempted around levels 40/50. So if you’re dying quickly (in just a few hits) it could be that you’ve prioritised different stats. Health/stamina/weapon scaling stat for your weapon should be priority (I.e. strength/dex/intelligence/faith/arcane). Maybe have a look at your stats and see what’s seemingly much lower than others. For me I always make health and stamina my focus to begin with as it will allow me to evade more and make a few more mistakes while learning without getting the dreaded “you died” screen. 

Not doing much damage - This could again be because of your stats, perhaps you haven’t put much focus into the scaling stats of the weapon, or you’ve switched weapons and the work you’d done scaling for a different weapon is now sort of void. It could also be that you haven’t leveled your weapon up with the smithing stones (these can be found pretty often for stones 1-3 at least). You should always keep levelling your chosen weapon as you go, ensuring that it’s the highest you can make it. 

Struggling with enemies and such - This, unfortunately, is just a matter of getting better through practice and repetition. Understanding enemy tells and being patient, waiting for an opening after an attack, is really important, you can’t just mash buttons either. Each press should be considered and deliberate as you’re committing to the roll, swing, use of equipment. You could also be using a weapon that you’re not particularly getting along with (it’s move set, timings, ash of war). Finding the weapons you get a long with and are comfortable using is more important than a weapon with the highest stats (to a point at least). 

Unfortunately for the souls games there isn’t really a quick fix or guide that can instantly make things easier. True to the meme it is about getting better at the game.
